---
title: "Reinforcement learning under partial observability"
description: >-
  Perceptual representations, memory, and attention in partially observable
  Markov decision processes.
---

::: {#key-ideas .callout-note title="Key ideas"}
- We use a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) as a biological
  model: an organism acts on sensory evidence and memory, not on direct
  knowledge of the world's state.
- Learning what an encoder retains and learning how often its outputs occur are
  different problems. The projects below study each in turn.
:::

## From observations to actions

The biological question is how an organism decides where to look or move
when its senses reveal only part of its surroundings. The encoder, memory,
and policy describe functions that a nervous system would need to perform,
without specifying the circuits that perform them.

A policy seeks to maximize expected cumulative reward. At time $t$, the
observation kernel $E$ gives the distribution of the observation given the
hidden state: $x_t \sim E(\cdot \mid s_t)$. After the agent chooses $a_t$,
the environment transition kernel $T$ gives the distribution of the next
state: $s_{t+1} \sim T(\cdot \mid s_t,a_t)$. The next observation is then
drawn from $E(\cdot \mid s_{t+1})$. For example, looking
away from an object removes it from view without necessarily removing it from
the scene.

In the models considered here, an encoder $F(z_t\mid x_t)$ represents the
current observation, and a memory $h_t$ summarizes earlier experience. A policy
chooses an action from $(z_t,h_t)$: it might look back toward the remembered
object even though the current view gives no indication of its location. This
internal state need not retain everything needed for an optimal decision.

## Research questions

- [Representation learning and efficient perceptual
  encoding](perceptual-representations.qmd): which distinctions should the
  encoder preserve, and at what cost? Predictive learning and reconstruction
  offer different training signals; a learned perceptual prior can reduce coding
  overhead for the distinctions retained.
- [Computational model of aesthetics](computational-aesthetics.qmd): given a
  useful encoder, which experiences should an agent seek to learn how often
  its outputs occur during a task? The model asks whether optimizing that
  sampling policy can explain preferences in movement and attention.
